subject: Maple Labs — promo settlement playbook and credit memo routing
messages:
From: Asha Nair <asha@maplelabs.com>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.com
Cc: billing@maplelabs.com
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: 30-day trial extension + credit memo to cover overage

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the onboarding session yesterday — the team ramped quickly. We're asking for a one-time 30-day extension on the promotional trial and a credit memo to cover $12,400 of overage charges that hit our invoice when we exceeded the free allowance. Finance is asking for the accounting treatment so they can close their month.

Can Redwood issue a proforma credit memo that we can use to offset the November invoice and confirm GL mapping (is the credit a contra-revenue item or an allowance?) and whether tax needs to be reversed? Attached the SOW with the requested extension language.

Appreciate your help,

— Asha
Billing Manager, Maple Labs
attachments: Trial_Extension_SOW.docx (docx)
From: mina_haddad@redwood.com
To: Asha Nair <asha@maplelabs.com>, billing@maplelabs.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-02T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: 30-day trial extension + credit memo to cover overage

Hi Asha — looping in Marcus from Finance to confirm ledger treatment and timing.

Short answers up front: we can issue a credit memo to offset the November invoice and set the trial extension flag for 30 days. For accounting: Redwood typically posts promotional credits as contra-revenue (account 4305) unless a customer requests to treat as an allowance/waiver with a different GLA; tax treatment depends on jurisdiction and whether the original invoice was taxed. For US domestic customers we normally reverse the taxable portion if the credit fully reverses billed usage.

Marcus — can you confirm the preferred journal entry for Maple Labs and whether we need to route a proforma to AP for their offset? Also, would you prefer a single credit memo for $12,400 or split into usage vs. promotional credit lines?

Next steps proposed:
- Redwood issues draft credit memo (proforma) for Maple to review (Action: Mina)
- Finance confirms GL mapping and tax reversal approach (Action: Marcus)
- Once approved, operations will post the credit and notify billing (Action: Marcus/Laure)

Thanks,
Mina
Sr. Revenue Operations Manager | Redwood Inference
From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: mina_haddad@redwood.com, Asha Nair <asha@maplelabs.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-03T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: 30-day trial extension + credit memo to cover overage

Thanks — quick accounting note.

For Maple Labs (US), recommended posting:
1) Create credit memo CM-ML-202611 for $12,400 with two lines: $9,800 usage reversal (revenue account 4010), $2,600 promotional allowance (contra-revenue 4305).
2) Tax: reverse the tax proportionally on the usage reversal line only. We'll record a tax adjustment journal (Sales Tax Clearing / Cash) to reflect the reversal.
3) AR offset: apply CM-ML-202611 to Invoice INV-ML-20261101 upon issuance.

If Maple prefers a single-line credit we can do that, but tax detail will be less explicit for their AP team. For month-end close cutoffs: if we post before 2026-11-10 EOD PT, it will clear in November financials; after that it will fall into December.

I can prepare the proforma PDF and route to AP for approval. Laura, can Ops create the credit in NetSuite once we get sign-off?

- Marcus
Manager, Revenue Accounting | Redwood Inference

Thanks Marcus — that split works for us and will make our AP reconciliation straightforward. We'd prefer the credit be issued this week if possible so November close is clean on our side.

One ask: can the proforma include the DocuSign link for internal approval? Our procurement team needs a signed acknowledgement for the adjustment. If you can add the SOW line that notes the 30-day extension, that helps our audit trail.

— Asha

Attachments: Maple_CredMemo_Draft.pdf; Trial_Extension_SOW.docx

Laura Bennett
